texts.preamble: Puttu Singh vs State Of M.P. on 13 February, 2017 1 Cr.R. No.711/2013 Puttu Singh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 16.02.2017 None for the applicant even in second round.
texts.facts: The matter is pending since the year 2013 and it appears that learned counsel for the applicant is not interested to argue the matter. Prosecution's case, in short, is that a sample of 'Khoya' was taken by the respondent - Food Inspector from the applicant and since it was found adulterated, the complaint was filed and trial was started. After considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the State, it would be apparent that before the appellate Court, an appeal was filed by the applicant and, therefore, the appellate Court could not pass any order which was against the applicant himself. If there was a defect of charge in the file by the trial Court then it was for the learned Sessions Judge to take suo moto revision against that order and an opportunity of hearing was to be given to the applicant separately and thereafter he could pass such an order to remand the case but instead of adopting such procedure, the learned Sessions Judge simply decided the appeal by remanding the case to the trial Court.
